hypsilophodon:enwiki:3.title: Hypsilophodon (First specimens and the debate of distinctiveness)

facts.statement: Hypsilophodon lived during the Early Cretaceous period.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Early Cretaceous,

facts.statement: The first remains of Hypsilophodon were discovered in 1849.
facts.quote: The first remains of Hypsilophodon were found in 1849

facts.statement: The type species Hypsilophodon foxii was named in 1869.
facts.quote: the type species, Hypsilophodon foxii, was named in 1869

facts.statement: Abundant fossils of Hypsilophodon were found on the Isle of Wight.
facts.quote: Abundant fossil discoveries were made on the Isle of Wight

facts.statement: Hypsilophodon had a pointed head with a sharp beak used for biting off plant material.
facts.quote: It had a pointed head equipped with a sharp beak used to bite off plant material, much like modern-day parrots

facts.statement: Hypsilophodon is traditionally classified as an early member of the group Ornithopoda, though recent research questions this classification.
facts.quote: It has traditionally been considered an early member of the group Ornithopoda, but recent research has put this into question

facts.statement: The first specimen of Hypsilophodon was recovered in 1849 from the Mantell-Bowerbank block.
facts.quote: The first specimen of Hypsilophodon was recovered in 1849, when workers dug up the soon-called Mantell-Bowerbank block

facts.statement: The species was named Hypsilophodon foxii, with the holotype being the skull discovered by William Fox.
facts.quote: The species was named Hypsilophodon foxii, and the holotype was the Fox skull

facts.statement: Huxley classified Hypsilophodon in the family Iguanodontidae, related to Iguanodon and Hadrosaurus.
facts.quote: Huxley classified Hypsilophodon taxonomically, considering it to belong to the family Iguanodontidae, related to Iguanodon and Hadrosaurus

facts.statement: The name Hypsilophodon means "Hypsilophus-tooth".
facts.quote: Hypsilophodon thus means "Hypsilophus-tooth"

facts.statement: The immediate reception to Huxley's proposal of Hypsilophodon as a distinct genus from Iguanodon was mixed.
facts.quote: Immediate reception to Huxley's proposal of a new genus, distinct from Iguanodon, was mixed

facts.statement: Most known specimens of Hypsilophodon were discovered between 1849 and 1921.
facts.quote: Most known Hypsilophodon specimens were discovered between 1849 and 1921

facts.statement: The known specimens represent approximately twenty individual animals.
facts.quote: These represent about twenty individual animals.

facts.statement: NHM R5829 is a significant specimen representing the skeleton of a large animal.
facts.quote: NHM R5829, the skeleton of a large animal

facts.statement: Specimens NHMUK PV R 5830 and NHMUK PV R 196/196a are skeletons of juvenile animals.
facts.quote: NHMUK PV R 5830 and NHMUK PV R 196/196a, both skeletons of juvenile animals

facts.statement: Specimen NHMUK PV R R2477 consists of a block containing a skull and two separate vertebral columns.
facts.quote: NHMUK PV R R2477, a block with a skull together with two separate vertebral columns.

facts.statement: A specimen was discovered in 1900 in the Black Hills of South Dakota, United States, by George Reber Wieland.
facts.quote: The specimen was found in 1900 in the Black Hills of South Dakota, United States, by George Reber Wieland

facts.statement: The species Hypsilophodon wielandi was named after George Reber Wieland, who discovered the specimen in 1900.
facts.quote: The specimen was found in 1900 in the Black Hills of South Dakota, United States, by George Reber Wieland, who the species was named after.

facts.statement: The specimen of Hypsilophodon wielandi comes from the Lakota Sandstone.
facts.quote: Geologically, it comes from the Lakota Sandstone.

facts.statement: Fossils found on the Isle of Wight are considered the only known authentic Hypsilophodon fossils.
facts.quote: This leaves the finds on Isle of Wight, off the south coast of England, as the only known authentic Hypsilophodon fossils.

facts.statement: Hypsilophodon fossils are found in the Hypsilophodon Bed, a marl layer in the upper Wessex Formation dating to the late Barremian, approximately 126 million years ago.
facts.quote: The fossils have been found in the Hypsilophodon Bed, a one-metre thick marl layer surfacing in a 1200 metre long strip along the Cowleaze Chine parallel to the southwest coast of Wight, part of the upper Wessex Formation and dating to the late Barremian, about 126 million years old.

facts.statement: A maximum length of 2.3 meters is often stated for Hypsilophodon.
facts.quote: For Hypsilophodon often a maximum length of 2.3 m is stated.

facts.statement: In 2009, Galton concluded that the largest femur previously attributed to Hypsilophodon actually belonged to Valdosaurus, reducing the maximum known length of Hypsilophodon to 1.8 meters.
facts.quote: However, in 2009, Galton concluded that this femur in fact belonged to Valdosaurus and downsized Hypsilophodon to a maximum known length of 1.8 m

facts.statement: Typical specimens of Hypsilophodon are about 1.5 meters long.
facts.quote: Typical specimens are about 1.5 m long.

facts.statement: In 2010, Gregory S. Paul estimated the weight of a 2-meter-long Hypsilophodon to be 20 kg.
facts.quote: In 2010, Gregory S. Paul estimated a weight of 20 kg for an animal 2 m in length.

facts.statement: Hypsilophodon was a bipedal dinosaur that ran on two legs.
facts.quote: Like most small dinosaurs, Hypsilophodon was bipedal: it ran on two legs.

facts.statement: The fifth finger of Hypsilophodon was opposable and could be used to grasp food items.
facts.quote: With Hypsilophodon the fifth finger had gained a specialised function: being opposable it could serve to grasp food items.

facts.statement: There is debate regarding whether the front teeth of Hypsilophodon had a specialized function, as most herbivorous dinosaurs had lost them by the Early Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Most herbivorous dinosaurs had, by the Early Cretaceous, become sufficiently specialized that the front teeth had been altogether lost (although there is some debate as to whether these teeth may have had a specialized function in Hypsilophodon).

facts.statement: The rear teeth of Hypsilophodon were fan-shaped.
facts.quote: The teeth to the back were fan-shaped.

facts.statement: The vertebral column of Hypsilophodon consisted of nine cervical, fifteen or sixteen dorsal, six or five sacral, and about forty-eight tail vertebrae.
facts.quote: The vertebral column consisted of nine cervical vertebrae, fifteen or sixteen dorsal vertebrae, six or five sacral vertebrae and about forty-eight vertebrae of the tail.

facts.statement: The back and tail of Hypsilophodon were stiffened by long ossified tendons connecting the vertebral spines.
facts.quote: Much of the back and the tail was stiffened by long ossified tendons connecting the spines on top of the vertebrae.

facts.statement: A long-held misconception was that Hypsilophodon was armoured.
facts.quote: A long-lived misconception concerning the anatomy of Hypsilophodon has been that it was armoured.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Hypsilophodon wielandi is a distinct species or synonymous with Camptosaurus valdensis.
facts.quote: Spanish Palaeontologist José Ignacio Ruiz-Omeñaca proposed that H. wielandi was not a species of Hypsilophodon but instead related to or synonymous with "Camptosaurus" valdensis from England

facts.statement: Many studies consider Hypsilophodon wielandi a dubious species, leaving H. foxii as the only valid species in the genus.
facts.quote: He, as well as other studies before and after Ruiz-Omeñaca's proposal, considered H. wielandi a dubious basal ornithopod, with H. foxii the only species in the genus.

facts.statement: Reports suggesting Hypsilophodon was present in the later Vectis Formation are considered unsubstantiated by Galton.
facts.quote: Reports that Hypsilophodon would be present in the later Vectis Formation, Galton in 2009 considered as unsubstantiated.

facts.statement: The first remains of Hypsilophodon were found in 1849.
facts.quote: Los primeros restos de Hypsilophodon fueron encontrados en 1849.

facts.statement: The type and only accepted species, Hypsilophodon foxii, was named in 1869.
facts.quote: La especie tipo y única aceptada, Hypsilophodon foxii, fue nombrada en 1869.

facts.statement: It lived during the early Cretaceous, approximately 124 million years ago in the Barremian stage, in what is now Europe.
facts.quote: que vivió a principios del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 124 millones de años, en el Barremiense, en lo que hoy es Europa.

facts.statement: It reached up to 1.8 meters in length, weighed about 20 kilograms, and was an agile runner.
facts.quote: Hypsilophodon alcanzó hasta 1,8 metros de largo, pesaba unos 20 kilogramos y era un corredor ágil.

facts.statement: It had a pointed head equipped with a sharp beak used to bite plant material, similar to modern parrots.
facts.quote: Tenía una cabeza puntiaguda equipada con un pico afilado que se usaba para morder material vegetal, como los loros modernos.

facts.statement: The skull structure, with teeth set far back in the jaw, strongly suggests it had cheeks to facilitate chewing.
facts.quote: The structure of its skull, with the teeth set far back into the jaw, strongly suggests that it had cheeks, an advanced feature that would have facilitated the chewing of food.

facts.statement: In 1882, Hulke suggested it was quadrupedal but also capable of climbing rocks and trees to seek shelter.
facts.quote: In 1882 Hulke suggested that Hypsilophodon was quadrupedal but also, in view of its grasping hand, able to climb rocks and trees in order to seek shelter.

facts.statement: In 1969, Peter M. Galton analyzed the musculoskeletal structure and showed the body posture was horizontal.
facts.quote: However, Peter M. Galton in 1969 performed a more accurate analysis of the musculo-skeletal structure, showing that the body posture was horizontal.

facts.statement: In 1971, Galton refuted Abel's arguments, showing the first toe was incorrectly reconstructed and concluding it was a bipedal running form.
facts.quote: In 1971 Galton in detail refuted Abel's arguments, showing that the first toe had been incorrectly reconstructed and that neither the curvature of the claws, nor the level of mobility of the shoulder girdle or the tail could be seen as adaptations for climbing, concluding that Hypsilophodon was a bipedal running form.

facts.statement: Fossils were likely accumulated in a single mass mortality event, suggesting the animals moved in large groups.
facts.quote: The Hypsilophodon fossils were probably accumulated in a single mass mortality event, so it has been considered likely that the animals moved in large groups.

facts.statement: Huxley originally assigned Hypsilophodon to the Iguanodontidae.
facts.quote: Huxley originally assigned Hypsilophodon to the Iguanodontidae.

facts.statement: In 1882, Louis Dollo named a separate family, Hypsilophodontidae.
facts.quote: In 1882 Louis Dollo named a separate Hypsilophodontidae.

facts.statement: In the modern view, Hypsilophodon is simply a basal ornithopod.
facts.quote: Hypsilophodon in the modern view thus simply is a basal ornithopod.

facts.statement: In 2017, Madzia, Boyd, and Mazuch reassessed Hypsilophodon outside of Ornithopoda, placing it as the sister taxon to Cerapoda.
facts.quote: In 2017, Daniel Madzia, Clint Boyd, and Martin Mazuch reassessed Hypsilophodon outside of Ornithopoda altogether, placing it in a more basal position, as the sister taxon to the Cerapoda

facts.statement: In 2023, Longrich et al. suggested that Vectidromeus and Hypsilophodon represented the only members of the Hypsilophodontidae.
facts.quote: In 2023, Longrich et al. described Vectidromeus as a new coeval genus of ornithopod closely related to Hypsilophodon. They suggested that Vectidromeus and Hypsilophodon represented the only members of the Hypsilophodontidae, since other taxa previously assigned to the group had subsequently been moved to other clades.

facts.statement: The genus authority is Huxley, 1869.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Huxley, 1869

facts.statement: The species authority is Huxley, 1869.
facts.quote: species_authority: Huxley, 1869.

facts.statement: Synonyms include Iguanodon foxii Owen, 1873 and Hypsilophodon foxi Zittel, 1890.
facts.quote: synonyms: Iguanodon foxii Owen, 1873 Hypsilophodon foxi Zittel, 1890

facts.statement: Hypsilophodon was a relatively small dinosaur, though not as small as Compsognathus.
facts.quote: Hypsilophodon era un dinosaurio relativamente pequeño, aunque no tan pequeño como, por ejemplo, Compsognathus.

facts.statement: Hypsilophodon could reach a height of up to half a meter.
facts.quote: Hypsilophodon habría alcanzado hasta medio metro de altura.

facts.statement: Like most small dinosaurs, Hypsilophodon was bipedal and ran on two legs.
facts.quote: Como la mayoría de los dinosaurios pequeños, Hypsilophodon era bípedo, corría en dos piernas.

facts.statement: Hypsilophodon had a lightweight, low skeleton with an aerodynamic posture, long legs, and a stiff tail immobilized by ossified tendons to maintain balance.
facts.quote: Un esqueleto liviano, bajo, con postura aerodinámica, patas largas y cola rígida, inmovilizada por tendones osificados, para mantener el equilibrio.

facts.statement: In Hypsilophodon, the fifth finger had a specialized function, being opposable and capable of grasping food.
facts.quote: En Hypsilophodon, el quinto dedo había adquirido una función especializada, ser oponible y podía servir para agarrar alimentos.

facts.statement: Despite having a beak like most ornithischians, Hypsilophodon retained five sharp triangular teeth at the front of the upper jaw.
facts.quote: A pesar de que tenía un pico como la mayoría de los ornitisquios, Hypsilophodon todavía tenía cinco dientes triangulares puntiagudos en el frente de la mandíbula superior, el premaxilar.

facts.statement: The upper jaw could hold up to eleven teeth, while the lower jaw could hold up to sixteen teeth.
facts.quote: La mandíbula superior llevaba hasta once dientes en el maxilar superior. La mandíbula inferior tenía hasta 16 dientes.

facts.statement: The teeth in the back of the mouth were fan-shaped.
facts.quote: Los dientes de la espalda tenían forma de abanico.

facts.statement: The skull of Hypsilophodon was short and relatively large, with a triangular, pointed snout ending in an upper beak whose cutting edge was notably lower than the row of upper teeth.
facts.quote: El cráneo de Hypsilophodon era corto y relativamente grande. El hocico era triangular y puntiagudo, terminando en un pico superior cuyo borde de corte era notablemente más bajo que la fila de dientes superiores.

facts.statement: A scleral ring of fifteen small bony plates supported the outer surface of the eye.
facts.quote: Un anillo esclerótico de quince pequeñas placas óseas apoyaba la superficie externa del ojo.

facts.statement: The vertebral column consisted of 9 cervical vertebrae, 15 or 16 dorsal vertebrae, 6 to 5 sacral vertebrae, and approximately 48 caudal vertebrae.
facts.quote: La columna vertebral consistía en 9 vértebras cervicales, 15 o 16 vértebras dorsales, 6 a 5 vértebras sacras y aproximadamente 48 vértebras caudales.

facts.statement: Much of the back and tail were stiffened by long ossified tendons connecting the spines on the top of the vertebrae.
facts.quote: Gran parte de la espalda y la cola estaban rígidas por largos tendones osificados que conectaban las espinas en la parte superior de las vértebras.

facts.statement: A long-standing misconception about the anatomy of Hypsilophodon was that it was armored.
facts.quote: Un concepto erróneo de larga data sobre la anatomía de Hypsilophodon ha sido que estaba blindado.

facts.statement: The idea that Hypsilophodon was armored was first suggested by Hulke in 1874 after finding a bone plate in the neck region.
facts.quote: Esto fue sugerido por primera vez por Hulke en 1874, después del hallazgo de una placa ósea en la región del cuello.

facts.statement: There is some debate over whether the front teeth of Hypsilophodon had a specialized function.
facts.quote: aunque existe cierto debate sobre si estos dientes pueden haber tenido una función especializada en el Hypsilophodon.

facts.statement: The genus Hypsilophodon was named by Huxley in 1870.
facts.quote: PBDB name: Hypsilophodon (genus), Huxley 1870

facts.statement: Hypsilophodon belongs to the parent group Hypsilophodontidae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Hypsilophodontidae

facts.statement: Hypsilophodon is classified in the family Hypsilophodontidae.
facts.quote: Family: Hypsilophodontidae

facts.statement: Hypsilophodon is classified in the class Ornithischia.
facts.quote: Class: Ornithischia

facts.statement: Hypsilophodon lived from the Kimmeridgian to the Aptian stages, between 154.8 and 119.57 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Kimmeridgian to Aptian (154.8 to 119.57 million years ago)
